speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Transport in light of the recent fatal accident in Tampines (a) how can LTA deter the occurrence of similar accidents in high traffic areas; (b) how can driver awareness and education on road safety be enhanced, particularly on speeding and reckless driving; (c) how can LTA minimise accident risks in future through road design and traffic management; and (d) whether there are plans to enhance data collection and analysis to better address current and future road safety challenges.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: asked the Minister for Transport pending investigations into the fatal accident in Tampines that occurred on 22 April 2024 (a) how will LTA improve the traffic safety provisions at this junction; and (b) what are the lessons learnt that can be pre-emptively applied to similar cross junctions islandwide to prevent similar tragic accidents in the future.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has addressed several questions raised by Members on road safety.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I will focus my response on road design and traffic management.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I would also like to assure Members and Singaporeans that road safety is and will continue to be a priority for the Ministry of Transport (MOT) and the Land Transport Authority (LTA).

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, our roads are designed in accordance with international safety requirements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms Poh asked about the safety provisions at the Tampines junction.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This junction is also designed in accordance with international safety standards, which includes sufficient line of sight for road users to see each other clearly, and appropriate road kerbs, lane and arrow markings installed conspicuously.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Second, LTA continues to review, develop and implement programmes that enhance road safety.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The work is ongoing and will extend to more traffic junctions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For School Zones, features include designated crossing facilities, coloured pavements, as well as traffic signs and markings.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: At primary schools, the speed limit is also lowered to 40 kilometres per hour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For Silver Zones, we implemented reduced speed limits and road safety measures such as narrower and meandering lanes, road markings, additional crossings and speed humps.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: More recently, we have rolled out the Friendly Streets initiative to make daily journeys to key amenities in neighbourhoods safer, more convenient and comfortable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Third, LTA leverages data from sources such as traffic accident reports from the Traffic Police (TP), as well as feedback from local communities and road users to design and implement localised road safety enhancements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Annually, LTA introduces about 1,000 of such enhancements across different parts of Singapore, including speed humps and three-dimensional road markings.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Beyond road design and infrastructure, LTA also conducts checks to ensure that the vehicles on our roads are roadworthy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They need to meet internationally recognised vehicle safety standards as well as undergo periodic inspections.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Enforcement will be carried out against errant vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: From 2021 to 2023, on average each year, LTA issued about 7,000 notices of offences for common illegal modification offences, conducted around 1,600 additional inspections and charged more than five workshops for violations.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also increased the penalties for illegal modification of vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We support MHA to educate and engage motorists on road safety practices.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As MHA said in the earlier reply, road safety is a shared responsibility, and we urge all road users to play their part, even as we do more to make our infrastructure safer for everyone.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Enhancing road safety involves safe roads, safe vehicles and safe road users.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The first supplementary question, Mr Speaker, is: I know MHA and LTA have done a lot of work to enhance the safety of our roads, but we want to make sure we do even more to save lives of students and school-going children, and of course our elderly.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I think most of us in this Chamber have primary schools, secondary schools or even junior colleges and polytechnics in our areas.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My first supplementary question is with regard to the use of data to assess riskier roads and accident-prone areas.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I would want to know if LTA can share whether there could be possibilities for the radius of the School Zones to be expanded; and whether there is any data to show that some of the accidents of our Singaporean parents who send their kids to school or who let their kids go to school every morning and come back from school by themselves, whether there are incidences of such accidents happening beyond the School Zones that we have designated.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned a number of those cases.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second is in regard to car modifications.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Senior Minister of State mentioned car modifications or speed enhancements, so whether she can share if these measures that LTA has introduced has led to, possibly, reduction in any of the speeding cases.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Regarding the expansion of the radius of the School Zones, this is something we will continue to monitor and review.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I do not think that there is a fixed one-size-fits-all kind of zone radius.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, it all depends on the local conditions – where the school is and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, it is something that we will continue to review.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regard to vehicle modifications, I do not have the numbers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But the thing is, you probably cannot directly correlate enforcement to illegal modifications with speeding and traffic accidents.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, an example will be that illegal exhaust modification poses a high risk and therefore, is a serious offence.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we do want to minimise or prevent such illegal modifications.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is why we have been stepping up the enforcement.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have stepped up the penalties since July 2021.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: I have a supplementary question and I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State what the proportion of fatal accidents is occurring at road junctions; and out of these fatalities, what is the proportion of pedestrians versus cyclists versus passengers and motorists?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
text: Following a very tragic fatal accident in Sembawang West last year, we have two of our junctions installed with the RAG arrows.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As regards the first question on accident statistics, I do not have the numbers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I will have to refer to MHA to get the numbers, with regard to the Member's question.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In relation to the second question, besides RAG, what else are we doing to enhance safety of cross junctions?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These are generally single right turn lanes, as well as turning onto one lane of oncoming traffic.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But after we have done the 200, we will continue to monitor and assess.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Beyond the RAGs, at cross junctions, there are a few things we have done or are still in the process of doing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, at traffic pockets, we put up "Give Way" signs to remind the turning motorists to look out for pedestrians.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are also adjustments to Green Men timings to give pedestrians a headstart in crossing the road.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And then, of course, we have the Green Man Plus scheme where the elderly and persons with disabilities can have a longer time to cross the road.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, we have recently started installing safety bollards at some signalised junctions where we assess there is a higher pedestrian risk, at selected corners of these junctions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: These safety bollards are what we call crashworthy bollards and they prevent errant vehicles from veering onto the footpath.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we will continue to look at ways to strengthen measures to enhance safety.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Does LTA have any plans to build more underground walkways, for example, from Tampines West MRT to Tampines Green Gem estate in my ward, so that pedestrians have a safer alternative to crossing busy junctions, like the junction where this horrific accident happened?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me say that for the junction at Tampines Avenues 1 and 4, which is the location of the accident, actually, there has been no feedback in relation to safety issues at that junction.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is the similar approach that we take for all locations where serious accidents have occurred.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, we always take into account the data we have, whether it is traffic accident reports from TP, data of incidents, whether it is injury-related or non-injury-related incidents on our expressways from the LTA monitoring team, as well as even data on road infrastructure which are frequently damaged or hit, which will give us some insights to the measures that we could put in place before any accidents happen.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And, of course, feedback from the local community, road users, the public, online and offline.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do data analytics and then identify locations where there are higher risks, to implement measures to enhance road safety.
With regard to the Member's specific question about underground walkways, it is the same with pedestrian overhead bridges (POBs).
We need to look at whether it is relevant and useful before we can implement them.
And if at-grade signalised traffic crossings are possible, then that is something we will go for because it is really a lot more effective and efficient.
But in certain areas where you cannot do at-grade signalised traffic crossings, say, because of the terrain or developments in the area, then we will do underground paths or POBs, for instance.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have a Parliamentary Question slated for tomorrow, which is similar and largely covered.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But I was hoping to ask if LTA would consider a comprehensive study of how we plan high-traffic areas, high-risk areas, especially around School Zones.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am sure many Members of this House, in our own constituencies, we face daily issues at the peak in the morning as well as at dismissal time, where traffic is hindered because the ingress and egress to some of our schools are in smaller lanes, creating inconveniences to residents as well as bottlenecks further upstream.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have seen some in my own estate, for example, where the cars would have to queue up into the bus spaces, creating additional difficulty for our transport operators.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In addition, these driver behaviours have been exacerbated, for example, this year, with a lack of bus drivers, earlier in the year, that has increased the number of parents who are sending their kids to school.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And secondly, because of the queues, it creates dangerous driver behaviour elsewhere as drivers are unable to turn, for example, into their housing estate, and they drive against traffic.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And in my own constituency as well, again —

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Mr Yam, get to your supplementary question, please.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: — we have seen a number of near misses.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State if LTA would be able to study this and also review the measures around School Zones?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And when there are School Zones, they also work very closely with the planning agencies, be it the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) and so on, to look at the traffic.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, traffic studies are actually conducted for such developments.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Having said that, yes, in certain school areas, for instance, you would experience congestion and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The reason for these issues may be a combination of many factors.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA works very closely with the school, with the Ministry of Education also, to address such issues at the ground level, because every School Zone area may be different and there are specific local conditions that we have to take into account.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some of the things we do is: we will work with the school and they will have, for instance, traffic marshals, traffic wardens that we work with; we give advisory to parents for gracious and good road safety behaviour.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also work with the schools to make sure that there are alternative parking or lay-by for the waiting vehicles, and to tell the parents not to wait along the roads illegally before dismissal time.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, these are various things that we do.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As regards whether we will do a study, actually we do continue to study this; and as I have said, we do traffic impact studies too.
